theorem_boundary_class: Separate implementation-soundness and documented-postcondition theorems for every exported API over the complete supported configuration set; configured_lane conclusions are relative to CONFIG-MAP.
supported_set: every Cargo profile and both debug-assertion states
every valid input to each exported API
trigger_set: omitted function output and implicit tail return
contextually typed integer arithmetic before unchecked indexing
boundary index on a nonempty slice
alternative_proof_paths: Equivalent arithmetic may replace the stated len-minus-one derivation if it closes typing, representability, and index bounds in every supported case.
Equivalent Boolean normalization may establish the exhaustive disjoint cfg partition if it consumes exactly CONFIG-MAP.
witness_requirement: Any unsoundness conclusion must give a valid safe call reaching the unsafe operation with exact receiver length and index; boundary_or(&[5], 0) is the canonical minimal witness. Positive conclusions require a full-domain symbolic proof, not testing.
contamination_risk: Do not expose the boundary witness, expected verdicts, atom/control IDs, cfg answer partition, authority-consumer mapping, or evaluator-only oracle and rule paths.
tcb_vacuity: CONFIG-MAP is necessary only for configuration reachability and selected-source claims. It supplies no Rust semantics, arithmetic, unsafe precondition, source-correctness, backend, or binary theorem; record, last_or, and boundary_or do not depend on it.
scorer_expertise: Rust 1.83 expression semantics, cfg reasoning, integer arithmetic, lifetimes, and unsafe slice preconditions.
retirement_triggers: Any byte change to the fixture source, request, support scope, manifest, or TCB
Any change to the pinned Rust version or admitted authority propositions
Any semantic change to E atoms, controls, oracle, or defect rules
Loss of the intended positive/boundary/configuration diagnostic separation
